\section[a promoção]{a promoção — the promotion; the special offer}

\label{lesson:PT-C360-promocao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the staff member, then the Portuguese for to delegate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a promoção}
\textbf{a promoção} — \textquotedblleft{}the promotion; the special offer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ela recebeu uma promoção depois de dois anos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She got a promotion after two years.}
\end{quote}

In shops, \emph{em promoção} — on special offer.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{promoção} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{prōmōtiō} \textquotedblleft{}advancement, promotion\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), from \emph{prōmovēre} \textquotedblleft{}to move forward\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{movēre} \textquotedblleft{}to move\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a promoção}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a promoção}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a promoção}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the staff member, then the Portuguese for to delegate, then say \emph{a promoção} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a promoção mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The promotion; the special offer\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[promover]{promover — to promote}

\label{lesson:PT-C360-promover}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to delegate, then the Portuguese for the promotion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: promover}
\textbf{promover} — \textquotedblleft{}to promote\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Promoveram o meu irmão a chefe de equipa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{They promoted my brother to team leader.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Ser promovido} — to be promoted. Also to promote an event.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{promover} comes from Latin \emph{prōmovēre} \textquotedblleft{}to move forward, to advance\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built from \emph{prō} and \emph{movēre} \textquotedblleft{}to move\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o cargo]{o cargo — the post, the position}

\label{lesson:PT-C360-cargo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the promotion, then the Portuguese for to promote.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o cargo}
\textbf{o cargo} — \textquotedblleft{}the post, the position\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ele ocupa um cargo importante na câmara.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He holds an important post at the council.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Ocupar um cargo} — to hold a post. \emph{A cargo de} — in charge of.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{cargo} is built on \emph{carregar} \textquotedblleft{}to load\textquotedblright{}, which is usually traced to Late Latin \emph{carricāre}, on \emph{carrus} \textquotedblleft{}a wagon\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short): a post is a load you carry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a qualificação]{a qualificação — the qualification}

\label{lesson:PT-C360-qualificacao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the post, then the Portuguese for the rise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a qualificação}
\textbf{a qualificação} — \textquotedblleft{}the qualification\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Para este trabalho, é preciso uma boa qualificação.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{For this job, a good qualification is needed.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Qualificações profissionais} — professional qualifications.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qualificação} is usually traced to Medieval Latin \emph{quālificātiō}, a learned word built on \emph{quālis} \textquotedblleft{}of what sort\textquotedblright{} and \emph{facere} \textquotedblleft{}to make\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
